angle.text: What to tell a mechanic before the work starts

copy.text: What to tell a mechanic before the work starts

scenes.why: The hook is the guide's own title: the question it answers, as a person would put it.

copy.text: Say what you're asking for, and nothing more.
Say the most you'll approve without a call.
Get every extra in writing before you say yes.
Keep the request, the estimate and the invoice together.

eyebrow.text: Before you hand over the keys

scenes.why: The guide's own checklist, the first sentence of each item, ticked in as it is read.

caption.text: Hand them a dated, mileage-stamped page saying what you are requesting today and that nothing else is authorized without a conversation first.

scenes.why: The turn: the product the guide itself hands over to, named and shown on its real screen, captioned with its listing's line closest to what the guide teaches. Screen: "Print" (The Service Boundary: a dated, mileage-stamped page you hand over before a shop touches the car, with what you're asking for and a limit.) chosen because it is the real screen closest to "Hand them a dated, mileage-stamped page saying what you are requesting today and"; focus on "What are you requesting today?".
Ends on where to read the whole guide, with the product beneath it: the viewer leaves with the next step, not only a pitch.

reasoning.because: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "gauge": a gauge sweeps, so scenes are revealed by a radial sweep.
Camera "float": a gentle float that keeps a held frame alive without demanding attention.
Grounds accent → light → light → accent: a warm accent, so light grounds lead and the accent is saved for the turns.
Sound-on placement: every transition, landing and reveal has a cue, and the bed ducks under the brand moment.
